key_insight: Single-crystal Ti-15Mo shows unexpectedly inverted elastic anisotropy and orientation-dependent yield onset that cannot be explained by simple CRSS/Schmid-factor models.
engineering_relevance: These orientation effects matter for texture-controlled processing of Ti-15Mo components because small changes in grain orientation can strongly alter stiffness, indentation yield, and deformation mode.
method: EBSD was used to identify the crystallographic surface normals of single grains.
Nanoindentation measured hardness, indentation modulus, strain-rate sensitivity, and yield onset near selected orientations.
Strain-rate-jump tests were used to estimate activation volumes and infer likely deformation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Across orientations near <111>, <124>, <011>, <023>, and <013>, modulus varied by about 10%, yield onset by 41%, and hardness by 6.6%, with activation volumes of 18–31 b^3.
watch_item: The mechanism assignment is suggestive rather than definitive, since the inferred role of retained athermal ω and the glide/twin separation are not directly proven by the indentation data alone.
paper_title: Orientation-Resolved Nanoindentation of Single Crystal Ti-15Mo: Inverted Elastic Anisotropy and Yield-Onset Behavior Beyond Simple CRSS Predictions
